title: Finance: Taxation
summary: Income tax with deductions, tax tables and rebates for different ages, medical tax credits, UIF, VAT, and interpreting payslips and tax certificates.

notes.title: Worked example 1
notes.problem: Mr Naidoo (aged 52) earns R38 500 per month and contributes R2 600 per month to a pension fund. He belongs to a medical aid with his wife and one child. Using the illustrative tables, calculate his annual tax.
steps: Pension deduction: 12 × R2 600 = R31 200; taxable income = R430 800
Less primary rebate: R95 598 − R17 500 = R78 098
notes.answer: R66 410 per year (about R5 534,17 per month)

notes.label: Exam tip
notes.text: Follow the order: annual income → subtract deductions → find the bracket → calculate tax → subtract rebates → subtract medical credits → divide by 12 if a monthly amount is required.

items: **VAT**: 15% on most goods and services; basic foods are zero-rated.
**UIF**: 1% of gross pay from the employee, matched by the employer (up to a maximum).
**Fuel levy**, **excise duties** (on alcohol and tobacco) and **property rates** (paid to municipalities).

notes.text: An **IRP5** tax certificate from the employer shows the year's income and the tax deducted. Taxpayers use it to complete their annual tax return with SARS.

notes.title: Taking VAT out of a price
notes.problem: An item costs R230 including 15% VAT. What is the VAT?
steps: The price is 115% of the price without VAT.
